restated: Let f(q,r) be the unique p such that (p,q,r) is a P-position of 3-row Chomp, defined by the Brouwer recurrence; for each fixed r let N(r) be the least q0 >= r such that the sequence f(q,r)-q is periodic for all q >= q0 (if row r has only finitely many P-positions, i.e. f(q,r) < q for all large q, N(r) is instead the least q with f(q,r) < q). Define B_c(a)=f(c+a,c)-(c+a) (undefined where no loser [c,a,b] exists), u_c=N(c)-c, p_c=the period of f(q,c)-q for q >= N(c) (p_c:=1 for rows with finitely many P-positions), q_r=lcm{p_c : 0<=c<r}, m_r=1+max{B_c(a) : 0<=c<r, a>=0}, U_r=max{u_c:c<r}, t_r=max(U_r,r). Then for every r>=1: (i) m_r<=r+1; (ii) p_r<=q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r); (iii) u_r<=max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r); (iv) q_{r+1}<=q_r^2(r+2)^(r+1). Hence N(r)<=r+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r) for rows with infinitely many P-positions, and N(r)<=r+1+max(t_r,m_r)+q_r(m_r+1)^(m_r) otherwise. Every quantity on the right is computed from the rows c<r alone, so this is an effective recursion for N(r).
